exposure: Birth characteristics (preterm birth, mode of delivery, birth weight, NICU admission)
Epilepsy characteristics (age of onset, duration, seizure type, frequency, control, neurological findings, EEG findings, aetiology)
Treatment modalities (polytherapy, surgery, ketogenic diet, drug therapy, specific Anti-Seizure Medication)
outcome: Birth characteristic profiles (prevalence of preterm birth, commonest mode of delivery, prevalence of normal birth weight, prevalence of NICU admission)
Developmental outcomes (prevalence of developmental delay, IQ assessment results)

Epilepsy characteristic profiles (commonest age of onset, duration, commonest seizure type, seizure frequency, seizure control status, prevalence of abnormal neurological findings, prevalence of abnormal EEG findings, commonest aetiology)
Treatment profiles (prevalence of polytherapy, surgery, ketogenic diet, drug therapy, commonest ASM)
cohort: A total of 98 children, aged 6-15 years, diagnosed with epilepsy of any aetiology and with a duration of at least six months, were included from the Outpatient Department or admitted ward of Dr. D. Y. Patil Medical College.
finding: The study characterized children with epilepsy as predominantly male, with high rates of preterm birth (86.7%), developmental delay (56.1%), and borderline IQ (59.2%), commonly presenting with focal onset seizures (67.4%) and structural aetiology (50%).
mod_finding: Normal vaginal delivery was the most common mode of delivery, occurring in 64.3% of the cohort.
birth_weight: Normal weight at birth (70.4% of subjects)
